# zonedb

> Query large datasets from any static host: no backend, no WASM, no HTTP Range requests. zonedb splits a large dataset into many small whole files at build time, builds indexes over them, and generates a typed TypeScript client that fetches only the files a query needs. Because it fetches whole small files (not byte ranges of one big file), it works on any dumb static host and every block is a plain, compressible, cacheable CDN object.

Key facts an implementer needs up front:

- Two packages, lockstep-versioned, neither with any runtime dependency: **`zonedb`** (browser runtime, ESM-only, production dependency) and **`zonedb-cli`** (Node build tool, devDependency, `bin` named `zonedb`).
- Install with pnpm: `pnpm add zonedb && pnpm add -D zonedb-cli`.
- The query API is the generated typed client only — a Prisma-style `where` object, not SQL and not a chained builder.
- Read-only from the browser: you update data by re-running `zonedb build` and redeploying. No cursors, no OR/AND/NOT in v1.0 (implicit-AND only).

## Quickstart

```bash
pnpm add zonedb && pnpm add -D zonedb-cli
npx zonedb init data/movies.ndjson   # guided wizard: reads your data, recommends what to index, writes zonedb.config.json
npx zonedb build                     # → public/zonedb/ (deploy this) + src/zonedb/{schema,client}.ts (commit these)
```

```ts
import { connect } from './zonedb/client'

const db = connect() // no args works for the standard deploy; connect({ basePath }) to override

const { records, hasMore } = await db.movies.findMany({
  where: { year: { gte: 2000 }, rating: { gt: 8 } },
  orderBy: { rating: 'desc' },
  limit: 20,
})
```

## Query API

- [Query guide](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/query-guide.md): the user-facing reference. Every operator with examples, null/absent semantics, list fields, sorting, pagination (`hasMore`, `total`, `maxResults`), `count`, `get`, query cost, error codes, and what the compiler rejects. Start here.
- [Query API surface (ADR-0001)](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/adr/0001-query-api-surface.md): the single canonical object/where-clause API. Methods per collection: `findMany(args) → { records, hasMore, total? }`, `count(args) → { count, exact }`, `get(id) → record | null` (PK-gated), `getSchema()`. `findMany({ signal })`, `count(where, { signal })` and `get(id, { signal })` take an optional `AbortSignal` that cancels the query's fetches and rejects with `ABORTED`. The runtime works unchanged in a Web Worker (use an absolute `basePath` there, since a relative one resolves against the worker script's URL), which keeps multi-MB block parsing off the main thread. Per-type operators on every non-json field (string `equals`/`not`/`in`/`startsWith`/`contains`/`endsWith`, plus `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` on a string sort field only; number & date `equals`/`not`/`in`/`gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`; boolean `equals`/`not`; multi-valued `some`/`every`/`hasEvery`/`isEmpty` — see ADR-0010; fields marked `nullable` add `isNull`/`exists` and fields marked `absent` add `isAbsent`/`exists`; the same flags make the generated record type `T | null` and optional). Filters that can't narrow which files are read are riders (ADR-0013): `not`, the missing-value operators, any filter on an unindexed field, and `contains`/`endsWith` without their index opt-in. A `findMany` `where` needs at least one filter that prunes (on the sort field or an indexed field), otherwise it's a compile error and a `NEEDS_PRUNING` runtime error. `contains` prunes only with 3+ characters, and an empty `startsWith`/`endsWith`, an empty `hasEvery` and `isEmpty: false` ride, which the types can't see; `wherePrunes(where, db.x.getSchema())` checks a runtime-built `where` without throwing (an empty `where` returns `true`, since it is allowed). `findMany({ where, scan: "block-order", limit })` opts a rider-only `where` into a walk over the data files in sort order that stops once the page is full; it needs a `limit` and no `orderBy` but the sort field, and a rare rider can still read most of the dataset. `orderBy` object (`asc`/`desc`, multi-key), offset/limit pagination, implicit-AND only.
- [Count, cost & pagination](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/adr/0008-count-cost-and-pagination.md): why `count` returns an approximate upper bound with an `exact` flag, and the limit+1 `hasMore` over-fetch.
- [Riders (ADR-0013)](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/adr/0013-riders.md): every field is queryable; an index decides only which filters prune. The manifest lists each field's `operators` and the `pruning` subset.
- [List operators](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/adr/0010-list-operators.md): `hasEvery` (contains all), `every` (every element matches; `[]` passes), `isEmpty` beside `some` on multi-valued fields; keys on one field AND, so exact-set is `hasEvery` + `every`. Absent/null lists match none of them. All prune via the index plus a per-field `emptyBlocks` list.

## Build & packaging (ADR-0005)

- [Package & CLI public contract](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/adr/0005-package-and-cli-contract.md): the two-package split, lockstep versioning, the `init`/`build`/`inspect` commands, flag-equivalence (`init --yes`), the committed `zonedb.config.json` (flags > config > inferred defaults), the two outputs, and the version compatibility handshake.
- [Codegen & typed client](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/adr/0004-codegen-and-typed-client.md): how the runtime and the generated per-dataset facade blend; what `createClient` / the generated `connect()` emit.
- [Runtime failure contract](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/adr/0007-runtime-failure-contract.md): `ZoneDbError` / `ZoneDbErrorCode`, partial-failure semantics, the fail-loud major-version mismatch at `connect()`, and the one retry: a 404 on a file the manifest names refetches the manifest (`cache: "reload"`) and reruns the query once if the manifest changed, so a stale cached manifest after a redeploy recovers on its own.

## Data format

- [Partitioning strategy](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/adr/0002-sharding-strategy.md): why many small whole files instead of one range-read file; content-hashed NDJSON blocks.
- [Index & manifest design](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/adr/0003-index-and-manifest-design.md): `manifest.json` as the stable entry point, zonemap sidecars, lazy inverted-index chunks, `formatVersion`.
- [Config JSON schema](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/packages/zonedb-cli/config.schema.json): the validated shape of `zonedb.config.json`.

## Examples

- [Movie catalog](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/tree/master/examples/movies): a complete build → deploy → query-in-browser app; see `src/zonedb/` for the generated client and `src/main.ts` for real queries.
- [Product lookup](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/tree/master/examples/products): a second dataset shape, same end-to-end flow.

## Optional

- [Deploy guide](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/docs/deploy-guide.md): caching headers for `manifest.json` (revalidate) vs the immutable content-hashed tree (cache-forever), and transport concerns per static host.
- [README](https://github.com/shivan2418/blockdb/blob/master/README.md): positioning, "use it when / reach for something else when", and the alternatives comparison (sql.js-httpvfs, DuckDB-WASM, hyparquet, PMTiles, Pagefind).
